approaches.name: Automated deposit insurance payout and single customer view system
approaches.description: The project funds IDIF software that automates insured-depositor compensation and gives access to bank deposit data for monitoring and payouts. Practices: Payout automation system for deposit insurance compensation; Single Customer View software for bank deposit data access.
approaches.why_innovative: New process: automated IDIF payout system replacing manual liquidation payouts | category Technological; adoption apply; judged in 1 round(s); final check: digital core, in_use before 2019

evidence.text: The proposed project will address the identified gaps in Individual Deposit Insurance Fund (IDIF)’s capacity to perform its mandate.4 IDIF reforms include increasing its recovery ratios in future payouts and incorporating lessons learned from the TSB and AIB payouts - namely, the need for further automation to hasten the payout process and for raising public awareness on the deposit insurance scheme.

extra_evidence.text: This subcomponent will fund the partial replenishment of IDIF’s reserves that backup funding arrangements from the government will complement,9 and with the remaining gap to be gradually closed by the inflow of industry contributions. • Subcomponent 1.2: Payout automation (US$1 million).

This subcomponent will provide IDIF with systems to access information on deposits from banks and monitor the banks’ deposit base (Single Customer View soft ware), 8 The World Bank provided technical assistance on deposit insurance until the end of 2019 and continues to provide technical assistance on the broader financial safety net to NBT focused on bank supervision and resolution.

category.rationale: Technological: payout automation software is the core mechanism

sector.rationale: Automating the deposit insurance fund's payout process is a public financial-sector administration function.
